facts.statement: Hintighernia is a newly described genus and species of tapejarid pterosaur from the Cretaceous of the Cambridge Greensand in the United Kingdom.
facts.quote: Notes: A member of the family Tapejaridae. Genus includes new species H. edingerae.

facts.statement: Hintighernia lived during the Early Cretaceous.
The genus Hintighernia and its species edingerae were formally named by Pêgas et al. in 2026.
Hintighernia is a tapejarid pterosaur from the Early Cretaceous Cambridge Greensand of the United Kingdom.
facts.quote: Hintighernia is a genus of tapejarid pterosaur from the Early Cretaceous of the Cambridge Greensand, United Kingdom.

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Hintighernia edingerae.
facts.quote: The type species is H. edingerae.

facts.statement: The species was named from a cranium that had previously been assigned to the genus Ornithostoma.
facts.quote: It was named from a cranium earlier referred to the genus Ornithostoma.

facts.statement: The generic name combines the Brittonic words hɨnt ("lord") and tɨɣern ("path"), translating to "Lord of the Paths".
facts.quote: The generic name is a combination of Brittonic hɨnt, "lord" and tɨɣern, "path", as a translation of the related genus Tapejara, the "Lord of the Paths".

facts.statement: The specific epithet edingerae honors German paleontologist Johanna Ottilie Edinger, founder of paleoneurology.
facts.quote: The specific name honours the German paleontologist Johanna Ottilie Edinger, the founder of paleoneurology.

facts.statement: The partial cranium CAMSM B54406, previously referred to Ornithostoma sedgwicki, is identified as a sinopterine tapejarid and assigned to Hintighernia edingerae.
Micro‑CT scanning shows that Hintighernia's neuroanatomy closely resembles that of Tapejara wellnhoferi.
Additional Cambridge Greensand remains are referred to Tapejaridae, and an isolated rostral fragment is tentatively assigned to cf. Hintighernia.
Ornithostoma sedgwicki is considered a chaoyangopterid azhdarchoid, known only from four jaw fragments.
Researchers suggest that a third, non‑azhdarchid azhdarchoid species may also be present in the Cambridge Greensand.
Europe is interpreted as an early hotspot of tapejarid phylogenetic diversity and a possible origin point for sinopterines in Eastern Laurasia and tapejarines in South America.

rejected.statement: Diagnostic features of Hintighernia include the shape of the upper temporal fenestra margins and a robust, elongate supraoccipital median ridge.
rejected.quote: Diagnostic traits, including the shape of the upper temporal fenestra margins and a robust, elongate supraoccipital median ridge, lead us to diagnose a new taxon, which we name Hintighernia edingerae gen. et sp. nov.
